newsitem.title: LATVIA: STOCKS MIXED, UNIBANKA, RTF REGAIN GROUND.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS MIXED, UNIBANKA, RTF REGAIN GROUND.

text.p: Latvian stock volumes slipped further on Wednesday with funds seen going into the first auction of two-year T-bills and privatisation certificates, dealers said.
Total volume was 92,000 lats against 114,000 lats and the Rietumu index rose 5.48 percent to 176.16.
The Saules Bank bourse index Saule10 closed 6.93 pct up at 151.08.
"A certain outflow of funds from the bourse can be seen," Leonid Ruderman, Parekss Bank dealer, told Reuters.
"The first two-year T-bill auction is expected to give a good yearly return of some 10 percent, which is better compared with p/e ratios of some 10 to 16," Ruderman said.
"A part of the funds are also being channelled into privatisation vouchers," he added.
Shares were mixed while some of the blue chips which registered losses in earlier sessions regained ground.
Unibanka jumped back to 3.50 lats from 3.14 lats on 26,200 lats and Riga Transport Fleet rose to 1.22 lats from 1.16 lats.
Valmiera Glassfibre and Daugavpils Chain led the secondary list as they slipped three and four santimes respectively.
Valmiera closed at 1.47 lats on 16,100 lats and Chain was down to 2.45 lats on turnover of 16,300 lats.
"Valmiera can be expected to lose further ground as the first quarter profit figure seems to be small for a company of Valmiera's size," one dealer said.
Valmiera earlier reported a first quarter profit of 269,300 lats.
Elsewhere on the secondary list Lode Brick maker fell to 2.47 lats from 2.51 lats on trade of 4,900 lats and Rigas Raughs yeast factory saw turnover of 4,000 lats
Raugs slipped to 3.87 lats from 3.89 lats.
Kaija fish cannery, currently in the process of joining the official list, lost seven santimes to 2.28 lats ahead of its shareholders' meeting on April 29. It traded 2,000 last worth of shares.
Elsewhere among fish canneries Salacgriva remained stable at 5.00 lats as it saw 3,300 lats worth of shares change hands.
Roja jumped to 2.77 lats from 2.41 lats on 2,800 lats of trade.
